q: A 13-year-old with testicular torsion ate 2 hours ago. What is appropriate?
o: Proceed without delay using an RSI or modified RSI
why: Surgery is time-critical to save the testis; do not delay for fasting.

q: What is usually discussed in consent for scrotal exploration?
why: The contralateral testis is usually fixed too.

q: What should be drawn up for cord traction?
why: Bradycardia and laryngospasm can occur with cord traction.

q: Which airway device is appropriate if the child is not fasted?
why: Cuffed ETT after RSI when not fasted.

q: Who can give consent for a 14-year-old who is not Gillick competent?
why: Consent comes from a person with parental responsibility.

q: Which is a delayed surgical complication of torsion?
why: Also testicular atrophy and wound infection.

q: Emergency treatment of a child can proceed without consent when:
o: The parents disagree with the surgeon
It is necessary to save life or prevent serious harm and consent cannot be obtained in time
